caption:
Ayat al-Kursi, the Verse of the Throne: Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence.

Surah Al-Baqarah (2:255). Swipe through for the Arabic, then English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese and Malay renderings.

Sources on the final slide.

sourcing.primary_text: Qur'an, Surah Al-Baqarah (2), Ayah 255 (Ayat al-Kursi, the Verse of the Throne)
sourcing.arabic: Uthmani script (edition quran-uthmani), api.alquran.cloud. Live-fetched and verified this session (2026-09-18) via GET /v1/ayah/2:255/editions/quran-uthmani,en.sahih,zh.jian,ko.korean,ja.japanese,ms.basmeih, HTTP 200.
sourcing.english: Saheeh International (edition en.sahih), api.alquran.cloud. Same live call as above, quoted verbatim including the translator's own bracketed interpolations '[all]' and '[presently]'.
sourcing.chinese: Ma Jian, 马坚 (edition zh.jian), api.alquran.cloud. Same live call as above, rendered verbatim with no corrections needed.
sourcing.malay: Abdullah Muhammad Basmeih (edition ms.basmeih), api.alquran.cloud. Same live call as above, rendered verbatim. Note for the audit trail only (no text altered): the raw string has a lower-case 'yang' opening the sentence that follows '...usahkan tidur.', which is the source's own styling, not a transcription artifact introduced here.
sourcing.korean: Edition ko.korean, api.alquran.cloud. Translator is listed as 'Unknown' in the source's own metadata (englishName field), so the on-slide credit says 'translator not specified by source' rather than inventing a scholar's name. The raw API string contained eleven stray mid-word/missing-word spacing artifacts, all closed up or inserted for the slide with no wording changed, consistent with the same edition's documented behaviour in quran-94-5.meta.json, quran-2-152.meta.json, quran-39-53.meta.json, quran-65-3.meta.json and quran-3-159.meta.json. Before -> after, verbatim: '없나니그분은' -> '없나니 그분은' (missing space inserted); '모 든' -> '모든'; '주관 하시도다' -> '주관하시도다'; '잠 도' -> '잠도'; '천 지의' -> '천지의'; '그 분의' -> '그분의' (both of its two occurrences); '것 을' -> '것을'; '대 하여' -> '대하여'; '그 것을' -> '그것을'; '아니하 시니' -> '아니하시니'; '장 엄하시노라' -> '장엄하시노라'. One further point left untouched on purpose: the raw text reads '권자가' where '권좌가' (throne) would be the expected word; since this is a wording difference rather than a spacing artifact, it was not changed and is rendered exactly as the API returned it.
sourcing.japanese: Edition ja.japanese, api.alquran.cloud. Translator is listed as 'Unknown' in the source's own metadata, cited on-slide as 'translator not specified by source'. Same live call as above, rendered verbatim with no corrections needed.
sourcing.candidate_selection_note: Ayah 2:255 (Ayat al-Kursi) was chosen as one of the most widely known and recited verses in the Qur'an, not yet covered by this channel (prior posts: 94:5, 2:152, 39:53, 13:28, 65:3, 3:159). Live-fetched and verified this session (2026-09-18); all six language editions came back complete on the first request, so no alternative candidates were needed.
sourcing.verification_note: All six language renderings came from a single live api.alquran.cloud request made this session (2026-09-18), not from memory or a prior file: GET https://api.alquran.cloud/v1/ayah/2:255/editions/quran-uthmani,en.sahih,zh.jian,ko.korean,ja.japanese,ms.basmeih, HTTP 200. See channels.json's ig-blankdiscussions._niche_note for why this project treats scripture sourcing as a hard requirement, not a style choice.
sourcing.compliance_check: Manually checked against scripts/data/compliance-policy.json's halal keyword-blocklists (intoxicants, pork, gambling, riba, immodesty, profanity, superstition, origins_patterns, animate_imagery, context_review) since compliance-gate.mjs does not cover this channel's schema. No blocklisted terms present in any of the six language texts; no imagery generated at all (pure typography slides). Content is a foundational statement on Allah's oneness and attributes (tawheed) - no context_review flags apply. Clean.
sourcing.layout_note: Ayat al-Kursi is markedly longer than this channel's typical single ayah. Added an optional 'fontScale' prop to IslamicCarouselSlide.tsx's text-slide variant (multiplies both fontSize and lineHeight, since a smaller font alone still overflows once line count is factored in) and applied per-language scale factors to slide-02 through slide-07 (ar 0.75, en 0.78, zh 0.9, ko 0.8, ja 0.82, ms 0.6 - Malay's translation runs to roughly 900 characters, by far the longest rendering of this ayah) to keep each language's full text inside the fixed 1080x1350 canvas instead of being cropped by the Frame's overflow:hidden. Chosen by character-count estimation, not a rendered visual check, since Desktop Commander (needed to run the actual Windows-side Remotion render) was unreachable (CONNECT_TIMEOUT) at the time this was written - MUST be visually verified once rendered, before publishing, and the scale factors adjusted if any slide still overflows or now looks too small.
sourcing.theme_note: This post introduces a 9th theme, 'ivory-cobalt' (warm ivory background with a cobalt-blue accent), added to src/compositions/IslamicCarouselSlide.tsx's THEMES/THEME_ORDER, since all 8 prior themes had each been used exactly once as of 2026-09-17 (obsidian-jade being the most recent). Per the component's own code comment, a new theme was added rather than repeating one.

renderCommand: npx remotion still src/compositions/registry.tsx IslamicSlide daily/2026-09-18/blankdiscussions/renders/quran-2-255-slide-NN.png --props=daily/2026-09-18/blankdiscussions/quran-2-255.slide-NN.json  (run once per slide, NN = 01 through 08)
